# Request Throttling

The F5 XC provider can retry backend throttling responses. Throttling is
disabled by default and is enabled only when the `throttling` block is present.

The retry policy applies only to HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` responses. It
does not retry other HTTP errors or transport errors.

## Enable Throttling

```terraform
provider "f5xc" {
  url = "https://<tenant>.console.ves.volterra.io/api"

  throttling = {
    max_retries         = 5
    initial_backoff     = "250ms"
    max_backoff         = "8s"
    multiplier          = 2.0
    jitter_ratio        = 0.2
    respect_retry_after = true
  }
}
```

Declaring an empty `throttling = {}` block enables the same default policy.

## Configuration Reference

| Argument | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_retries` | `5` | Retry attempts after a 429 response. A value of 5 permits up to 6 total attempts. |
| `initial_backoff` | `"250ms"` | Delay before the first retry. |
| `max_backoff` | `"8s"` | Maximum exponential-backoff delay. |
| `multiplier` | `2.0` | Backoff growth factor. Must be at least `1.0`. |
| `jitter_ratio` | `0.2` | Randomized delay range. Must be between `0` and `1`. |
| `respect_retry_after` | `true` | Use the backend `Retry-After` value when supplied. |

The provider uses exponential backoff with jitter and caps waits at
`max_backoff`. When `respect_retry_after` is enabled, a valid `Retry-After`
header takes precedence. Retry waits honor Terraform cancellation, and a 429
cooldown is shared by concurrent requests for the same resource key.

## Production Guidance

- Enable throttling for automated workloads that can make concurrent API calls.
- Keep `respect_retry_after = true` unless directed otherwise by F5 support.
- Start with the defaults; increase `max_retries` only when the pipeline can
  tolerate longer applies.
- For large configurations, reduce Terraform Core concurrency, for example:

```sh
terraform apply -parallelism=5
```

- Treat persistent 429 responses as a capacity or workload-design signal. Do
  not rely on retries alone to resolve sustained request pressure.
